pictures.scene: Jean Simeon Chardin, The Young Schoolmistress - the girl in the red ribboned cap leaning in over the desk with the long needle held out to a letter on the open page, the small child in the patterned cap bent close over the book with both hands flat on the desk, the plain warm brown wall standing quiet above them, You are good to Your servant O LORD according to Your word, teach me good judgment and knowledge for I believe in Your commandments
pictures.name: pd_chardin_onderwijzeres

pictures.scene: Victor Westerholm, Market Lighthouse - the red and white banded light standing up alone on the bare grey rock with its lantern catching the last of the sun, the little yellow storehouse and the tackle beside it, the wide pale evening sky filling everything above, before I was afflicted I went astray but now I keep Your word, You are good and You do what is good, teach me Your statutes
pictures.name: pd_westerholm_vuurtoren

pictures.scene: Paul Delaroche, Cardinal Beaufort Interrogating Joan of Arc in Prison - the girl sitting on the straw of her cell with her hands bound in her lap and her head turned away from them, the cardinal leaning down over her in his red robe pressing his question, the dark stone of the prison closing over the whole scene, though the arrogant have smeared me with lies I keep Your precepts with all my heart, their hearts are callous and insensitive but I delight in Your law
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Pekka Halonen, The Mowers - the barefoot man out in the tall grass swinging the scythe through it with his shirt sleeves rolled back, the second mower working on behind him, the cut swathes lying bright in the summer light all down the slope, it was good for me to be afflicted that I might learn Your statutes, the law from Your mouth is more precious to me
pictures.name: pd_halonen_maaiers

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Still Life with Bible - the big open Bible standing heavy on the table with its pages spread and the brass candlestick beside it burnt out, the small worn yellow book lying down in front of it, the dark wall behind, than thousands of pieces of gold and silver
pictures.name: pd_gogh_bijbel

lines.text: You are good to Your servant, O LORD,
Teach me good judgment and knowledge,
for I believe in Your commandments.
Before I was afflicted, I went astray;
but now I keep Your word.
You are good, and You do what is good;
Though the arrogant have smeared me with lies,
I keep Your precepts with all my heart.
Their hearts are callous and insensitive,
but I delight in Your law.
It was good for me to be afflicted,
that I might learn Your statutes.
The law from Your mouth is more precious to me
than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.
